Info-post on the Tomb of the Unknown and the Guards who stand watch over it

Thanks. Great images and really appreciated that you added the context.

I live in Ottawa, two blocks from the Canadian National War Memorial. In true Canadian fashion, we are a little more relaxed than the boys at Arlington. I like having the NWM right in the heart of the city though, much higher profile than tucked into a peaceful plot.

We only added the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier to the NWM in 2000 and have had some issues. We added the honour guard after an incident where someone urinated on the tomb in 2006, but subsequently dialed back the hours and made it seasonal. We often see -30C here in the winter and that duty would be cruel and unusual punishment.

Last year one of the honour guards was shot and killed while on guard. Terrorist attack or mental health failure depending on which narrative you subscribe to. The guards continue stand with weapons unloaded, but now have a protective police detail.

Numbers dont lie: Its time to build your own router
I wonder how does the power consumption compare

I built one with a cheap AM1 system running Linux. It pulls about 25w idle and under full load (which basically never happens) it pulls 50w. I bought a used quad port PCIe Intel ethernet card to go with it and it draws a lot of power compared to the rest of the system. I wouldn't use an old PC for this because of power consumption, but a small form factor AMD AM1 or an Intel Atom isn't bad. It can also double as an HTPC as well as running other web based services. I use owncloud and also store my music collection on it and mount the directory when I'm gone over ssh so I can have my music library anywhere with internet. You also get the added benefit of things like iptables for a firewall. I ran a server version of linux and set up routing via iptables myself but most people just run pfsense.

Thanks, I'll have to set that up. I use Linux the vast majority of the time so I can mount it in Linux and it works just like a local directory even over the net, but I have been wanting something to stream from my phone to my car stereo and this looks like it'll actually work. I guess that's why I've been struggling to find a good sshfs client for android, Plex exists.
Have fun! I use it in my car with my Bluetooth receiver and its perfect.

FreeSCO: Build A Router With A 386 And A Floppy Disk http://www.enterprisenetworkingplanet.com/netos/article.php/1107911/FreeSCO-Build-A-Router-With-A-386-And-A-Floppy-Disk.htm

I went full nerd on this particular task last year.

I bought a Dell r410 with an extra ethernet card and populated the drive bays with 2 TByte drives. I installed ESXI, and I administrate from my desktop. I created a virtual machine and installed OpenWRT from an image and that's my router. I built another virtual machine (Vortexbox) to serve my music and video. The whole mess works nicely.

I am inclined to try to figure out XEN, that will have to wait until better RAID cards are cheaper. This machine is working well. I know it could have less power draw, but I live in Wisconsin. A little extra heat in the basement isn't going to kill anyone.
